approved_findings: The same canonical URL remains an API guide to Visa CE 3.0 dispute evidence. Both captures require Visa network reason 10.4, two paid undisputed non-validation transactions using the same payment method 120-364 days earlier, descriptions for all three, merchandise_or_services, and the specified cross-transaction evidence-element match; device fingerprint plus device ID is invalid (old lines 12-30; new lines 13-31).

Both captures describe evidence.enhanced_evidence.visa_compelling_evidence_3, enhanced_eligibility_types, and evidence_details.enhanced_eligibility.visa_compelling_evidence_3 with required_actions and status (old lines 32-103; new lines 33-104). Example JSON differences are punctuation/formatting, not object behavior.

The submission path is unchanged: requires_action identifies missing evidence, qualified means ready to submit, submit=false saves without submission, and ineligible CE 3.0 evidence still submits via the standard path with not_qualified status. Overall dispute status must be tracked separately; standard evidence is advised for fallback if CE 3.0 is disapproved (old lines 112-125; new lines 113-126).

The testing section changes 'test environment' to linked 'sandbox' wording (old lines 137-139; new lines 138-140). Both say any two test transactions can be used as prior_undisputed_transactions there without payment-method/date validation; primary and secondary evidence elements still receive Visa CE 3.0 validation, and CE status does not determine overall won/lost status (old lines 139-152; new lines 140-153). This wording change does not establish new production eligibility or account access.

The November same-URL delta is still non-substantive: heading whitespace, emphasis, table padding, JSON punctuation, and test-environment-to-sandbox terminology. However, current source line 72 says 'Stripe autofills when eligible,' which can be read as a guarantee of complete automatic evidence. Both old raw line 108 and new raw line 109 say Stripe attempts to autofill the disputed transaction and prior-transaction evidence when it identifies CE 3.0 eligibility, and manual CE 3.0 evidence may still be added. A query asking whether eligibility guarantees complete autofill would be answered misleadingly by the source. Recommend a narrow source correction to use 'attempts' and preserve manual addition; Stripe must have processed all prior undisputed transactions (old line 110; new line 111).
approved_conflicts: Current source line 72 says Stripe autofills when eligible, while both raw line 108 (May) and line 109 (November) say Stripe attempts to autofill and lets the business manually add CE 3.0 evidence; the source should not imply complete autofill is guaranteed.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the same Visa 10.4, two prior transactions 120-364 days earlier, same payment method, paid/undisputed/non-validation, product descriptions, category, and evidence matching prerequisites (old lines 12-30; new lines 13-31).

Keep CE qualification distinct from dispute outcome: not_qualified can still mean evidence was submitted through standard dispute flow, while won/lost belongs to overall dispute.status (old lines 121-125, 150; new lines 122-126, 151).
Keep the testing-only exception limited to prior transaction identity/date validation; primary and secondary evidence-element checks remain (old lines 137-143; new lines 138-144).
Keep the shared attempted-autofill and manual-addition qualification: eligibility does not guarantee complete autofilled evidence (old lines 108-110; new lines 109-111).
unresolved_questions: The captures describe eligibility and testing mechanics, but do not verify that a particular dispute qualifies, that an issuer accepts CE 3.0 evidence, or that the business wins.
The page's sandbox wording does not prove a merchant has sandbox access or establish any production relaxation of the 120-364-day and same-payment-method criteria.
